title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this page and its neighbours: Ĝ is a profinite group, a quotient of the profinite modular-type group Ĝ_{0,3}^{+∧}, i.e. essentially (P)SL(2,ℤ)^ = ℤ/2 * ℤ/3 completed. It has two distinguished elliptic generators:
- ρ (order 3 type);
- σ (involution, σ^{-1}=σ).
The product ε_0 = σ^{-1}ρ generates a procyclic 'cusp' (inertia) subgroup L_0. Its conjugate L_1 = σL_0σ^{-1} is generated by ε_1 (the marginal t_1).

A group M[0] acts on Ĝ. It lies in a larger group M that carries a multiplier character χ: M → Ẑ^*. M[0] comes with two functions α, β: M[0] → Ĝ such that:
- u(ρ) = int(α)ρ and u(σ) = int(β)σ, i.e. u fixes the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ.

Putting ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} = [α,ρ] and η = [β,σ], one gets:
- u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ, i.e. ξ = [u,ρ] = u(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = [u,σ].
- ξ = η ε_1^ν with ν = (μ-1)/2 ∈ Ẑ, where μ is the multiplier of u. This is inherited from Ĝ_{0,3}^+.

Points made on this page:
(i) α, β are determined only up to the centralizers of ρ and σ. If M[0] does not act faithfully on Ĝ, they need not descend to the image M'[0] = Im(M[0] → Aut(Ĝ)). By contrast, ξ = u(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = u(σ)σ^{-1} depend only on the automorphism induced by u, so they are defined on M'[0].
(ii) M'[0] lies in Norm_{Aut(Ĝ)}(L_0). One gets a map M'[0] → {solutions (ξ,η) of (26)}. Forgetting the exact exponent, (26) is recorded in the weaker form η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1. Grothendieck notes the exact exponent ν = (μ-1)/2 is retained if Ĝ is large enough that Ĝ_{0,3}^{+∧} → SL(2,ℤ)^/±1 factors through Ĝ, and he assumes this.
(iii) He defines (32) Σ_{Ĝ,ρ,σ} ⊂ Ĝ×Ĝ as the set of pairs (ξ,η) with:
  1) ξρ conjugate to ρ;
  2) ησ conjugate to σ;
  3) η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1, i.e. ξ = ηε_1^{ν'} for some ν' ∈ Ẑ.

The crossed-out lines and the next page complete the argument. For u ∈ Aut(Ĝ), conditions 1) and 2) say that u fixes the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ. Condition 3) is computed as η^{-1}ξ = σ(u(ε_0)ε_0^{-1}), which lies in L_1 iff u(ε_0) ∈ L_0, i.e. iff u normalizes L_0. So the group B̃'_0 of automorphisms that preserve the classes of ρ and σ and normalize L_0 embeds into Σ via u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ]), injectively when ρ and σ generate Ĝ.

Purpose: a 'loop-equation' (équation des lacets) parametrization of the Galois/GT-type automorphisms of the profinite modular group by commutator pairs, cut out by conjugacy and inertia conditions. It is the genus-0, three-point/modular analogue of the Drinfeld–Ihara (λ,f) description of GT.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One terminological slip: (32) calls (ξ,η) 'conjugué', but the condition is that ξρ (not ξ) is conjugate to ρ, as the next page makes precise.

Weakening (26) to η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1 loses the link between ν' and the multiplier μ. Grothendieck explicitly acknowledges this and patches it by an extra assumption on Ĝ, so it is a gap that is flagged rather than an error.
Injectivity of the map u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ]) requires that ρ, σ topologically generate Ĝ. This hypothesis is added only on the next page.

ideas.what: ξ=[u,ρ] and η=[u,σ] depend only on the image of u in Aut(Ĝ), while the 'conjugators' α, β need not descend when the action is non-faithful (they are ambiguous up to centralizers)
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle/parameter descent to the image in Aut; centralizer ambiguity in Ihara-type parametrizations

ideas.what: Set Σ of pairs (ξ,η) with ξρ~ρ, ησ~σ, η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1 (the cusp inertia), as a parameter space for automorphisms of the profinite modular group
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of 'inertia-preserving' / special outer automorphisms of PSL(2,ℤ)^ (GT-type action on the profinite modular group, M_{1,1}/M_{0,4} level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (modular group/M_{1,1} level)
ideas.where_published: Related ideas in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT), but not this explicit set

ideas.what: Normalizing the cusp subgroup L_0 is equivalent to η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1 (finished on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preservation condition for automorphisms of a profinite surface/orbifold group

ideas.what: Exponent relation ξ = ηε_1^{(μ-1)/2}, linking the parameter to the cyclotomic multiplier
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of the λ-dependence in the GT hexagon/2-cycle relations (the (λ-1)/2 exponent)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's independent, pre-Drinfeld-style 'loop equation' parametrization of automorphisms of the profinite modular group by commutator pairs (ξ,η) = ([u,ρ],[u,σ]). The pairs are cut out by conjugacy-class and cusp-inertia conditions, and the exact exponent (μ-1)/2 is kept by requiring Ĝ to dominate SL(2,ℤ)^/±1. This documents his own route to GT-type objects, but the content parallels known work (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps).
missed.quote: On a ainsi une application (ξ,η) d'un certain sous-groupe M'[0] ⊂ Norm_{Aut(Ĝ)}(L_0) dans l'ens. des solutions de l'équation en ξ,η
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's own route to GT-type equations at the level of the modular group. Mathematically it is close to known parametrizations, so it is of limited novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine set-up step: definition of the parameter set and descent of ξ, η to the image in Aut. It belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type 'loop equation' work, which is historically interesting, but the mathematics mirrors Drinfeld/Ihara-style parametrizations known in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Top-right marginal formula: should read [α,ρ] = αρ(α)^{-1} (consistent with (23) ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}), not '[α,β] = αβ(αβ)^{-1}'.
In (32) condition 3), the generator is ε_1 (the t_1 of (26)), giving ξ = ηε_1^{ν'}.

'relation qui rend que [?] ... si on suppose {+pas.+} M̂ assez gros': the sense is that the relation loses the precise exponent ν unless Ĝ (not M̂) is assumed large enough that Ĝ_{0,3}^{+∧} → SL(2,ℤ)^/±1 factors through Ĝ. The insertion 'pas' indicates a negation ('si on ne suppose pas').
The target written over the arrow is most likely SL(2,ℤ)^ modulo ±1 ('SL(2,Ẑ)/2' in the image denotes the quotient by {±1}).
Condition 1) of (32) should read 'ξρ conjugué à ρ' (i.e. condition on ξρ), and condition 2) 'ησ conjugué à σ'.
